legend.local: Feature exists locally/legacy, not confirmed on shared module

libraries.name: Auth v1.3
libraries.purpose: Canonical shared authentication SDK plus reusable multi-variant account UI, migration safety, sessions, roles, passkeys and audit integration.
libraries.notes: Current immutable release: 1.3.0. Authentication Lab keeps the original full technical test page. The Shared account UI card now compares flow variants and independent Airy/Glass/Warm/Midnight/Playful themes, with modal and in-app previews. Classic remains the default flow.

libraries.name: Apps Auth / canonical identity
libraries.purpose: Stable cross-app device identity plus app-user identity bridging for monitoring and future central authentication.

libraries.name: Passkey Auth
libraries.purpose: Reusable WebAuthn/passkey client framework for private administrator surfaces.

libraries.name: Account UI
libraries.purpose: Reusable account/profile controls and account-facing UI plumbing.
libraries.notes: Central module exists; consumer coverage has not yet been fully audited.

libraries.name: App Monitor tracker
libraries.purpose: Cross-app session, device, activity, identity and traffic telemetry into the App Monitor backend.

libraries.name: Firebase Usage Monitor
libraries.purpose: Application-side ledger for attributed Firebase/Firestore reads, writes, deletes and listeners by app/project/device.
libraries.notes: Tracks attributed reads/writes/deletes/listeners with daily thresholds plus shared 5-minute burst warnings (defaults: 200 reads / 50 writes) to surface runaway loops quickly; thresholds remain app/device configurable.

libraries.name: Version Lab (full shared system)
libraries.purpose: Developer-only managed release system derived from the Beyond100 reference: central comparison UI, immutable checkpoint capture, snapshots, Git source history, compatibility metadata and AI/reusable workflow contracts.
libraries.notes: Full shared system is built but intentionally not installed in a consuming app yet. Beyond100 is the reference/full bespoke implementation; Openday uses the earlier thin shared v1; Snag has version history/archive. Next step is trial installation on an app with no prior Version Lab.

libraries.name: Privacy
libraries.purpose: Shared privacy preference storage/events and opt-in gates for optional analytics or personalised monitoring.
libraries.notes: Library exists; app-by-app consumer audit still required.

libraries.name: Billing
libraries.purpose: Provider-neutral browser billing client with app-supplied entitlement and authenticated billing adapters.
libraries.notes: Library exists; no verified production consumer recorded yet.

libraries.name: Pronunciation coach
libraries.purpose: Reusable microphone waveform, reference audio, speech comparison, rhythm/intonation analysis and pronunciation-scoring UI.

libraries.name: Notifications v1.1
libraries.purpose: App-independent notification event, policy, recipient-preference, delivery-method and reusable UI capability with role/user overrides, cost governance, push registration and provider adapters.
libraries.notes: Notifications v1.1 is installed in the standalone Lab, App Monitor, Snag and Openday. Openday uses a thin private-state adapter with the existing memorable-token sync: in-app inbox/preferences are live, while browser push remains setup-required until Openday has a trusted authenticated server transport for FCM registration/delivery. Snag continues to use its authenticated Firebase/R2 adapter.

libraries.name: PWA v1.0
libraries.purpose: Shared installability, service-worker, standalone-mode, update/offline and iOS Home Screen readiness capability for the Apps portfolio.
libraries.notes: PWA v1 installations across the main portfolio were explicitly accepted on 5 Oct 2026 as assumed working, subject to periodic app audits. Installed does not imply Notifications is installed.

libraries.name: Apps Platform v1.5.0
libraries.purpose: Versioned integration layer and lazy capability loader that keeps shared infrastructure separate from consuming app business logic.
libraries.notes: Apps Platform v1.5.0 exposes Notifications, PWA and Shared Notes & Annotations as canonical shared capabilities while keeping consuming-app business logic outside shared modules.

libraries.name: Shared Notes & Annotations v1.0
libraries.purpose: Shared developer notes, feedback and element-linked annotations with drafts, review queue, implementation history and optional transport hooks.
libraries.notes: Created from the strongest patterns in Beyond100, Snag, LearnLatin, Next and Openday. TouchType is the intended first clean consumer; existing bespoke implementations remain local until deliberately migrated.

libraries.name: Learning SDK
libraries.purpose: Shared learners, curriculum, learning events, mastery, assessments and spaced-repetition model for learning apps.

libraries.name: Shared Data / Firebase adapter
libraries.purpose: Common data access, sync, instrumentation, retries and project configuration layer so apps do not independently wire Firebase.

libraries.name: Shared UI / panel system
libraries.purpose: Reusable cards, draggable/reorderable panels, dashboard layout and common interface controls.

libraries.name: Release Gate & App Validation
libraries.purpose: Shared recursive syntax/data/asset validation, browser smoke tests, app-specific regression scenarios, sync quiescence checks, resource/Firebase budgets, CI reports and bounded load-testing tools.
libraries.notes: Reference integration: Openday. Shared engine lives in Apps; consuming apps provide only config and app-specific fixtures/invariants. Recommended flow: validation/preflight -> shared gate -> promote exact passed SHA -> CI repeat -> deploy. Load testing blocks production unless explicitly opted in.

libraries.name: Diagnostics / error reporting
libraries.purpose: Common client diagnostics, structured errors, health reporting and operational troubleshooting hooks.

infrastructure.name: Cloudflare deployment credentials
infrastructure.purpose: GitHub Actions credentials used to deploy shared Cloudflare Workers. Secret values are never stored in this register.
infrastructure.notes: Verified: Snag's GitHub Actions secrets provide CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID for the delegated shared App Monitor Worker deployment. Apps owns the Worker source; Snag is the credential host.

infrastructure.name: Notification provider credentials
infrastructure.purpose: Server-side credentials used by the shared Notifications service for push, email, SMS, WhatsApp and messaging providers.
infrastructure.notes: Provider credential ownership is separate from consumer adoption. FCM authority is held by Kk-syllabus; Snag may act as a deployment/credential bridge for the shared Worker, but this does not mean Snag consumes Notifications. Consumer installation is tracked only in the shared-library adoption map.

infrastructure.name: Cloudflare Workers
infrastructure.purpose: Server-side runtime for shared/app APIs and notification delivery.
infrastructure.notes: App Monitor Worker source lives in Apps and is deployed by the delegated workflow in Snag.

infrastructure.name: Cloudflare R2
infrastructure.purpose: Object storage used by Workers for app data, telemetry and notification inbox/audit records.
infrastructure.notes: Verified App Monitor binding: APP_MONITOR_DATA -> apps-monitor-data. Snag also uses R2 for app/media storage.

infrastructure.name: Firebase / Firestore backend
infrastructure.purpose: Firebase projects and Firestore databases used by apps for application data and shared monitoring.
infrastructure.notes: Snag uses its own Firebase project; older apps may still use kk-syllabus. This row tracks platform use, not secret values. Remaining app/project mappings should be audited progressively.

infrastructure.name: Firebase Authentication
infrastructure.purpose: Firebase user authentication where a consuming app uses Firebase Auth.
infrastructure.notes: App Monitor deliberately uses its existing passkey/session system instead of Firebase Auth. Other app coverage is recorded only when verified.

infrastructure.name: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)
infrastructure.purpose: Potential shared browser/mobile push provider for Firebase-backed apps.
infrastructure.notes: FCM is the approved/default browser-push provider. Firebase authority is Kk-syllabus. App Monitor and Snag consume FCM through shared Notifications. Snag also hosts/delegates parts of the Cloudflare deployment path; deployment ownership and app consumption are deliberately represented separately.

infrastructure.name: GitHub Actions
infrastructure.purpose: Release gates, validation and deployment workflows.
infrastructure.notes: Usage varies by repository. Shared Worker deployment may be delegated to a credential-host repository.

infrastructure.name: GitHub Pages
infrastructure.purpose: Static hosting for Apps and consuming web apps.
infrastructure.notes: Static front ends are deployed separately from Cloudflare Worker backends; release checks must verify both where an app uses both.

infrastructure.name: OneSignal
infrastructure.notes: Not approved and not active. Removed from the default Notifications runtime. Reintroduction requires explicit third-party review and approval.

adoptionLegend.available: Shared capability exists and may be considered for this app; this does not authorise an app change.
adoptionLegend.compatible: Compatibility has been verified without installing the shared capability.
adoptionLegend.installed: The app repository has been explicitly modified to consume the shared capability.
adoptionLegend.local: The app has a local/legacy implementation, not the shared capability.
adoptionLegend.unavailable: Not currently available for this app.

activationLegend.available: The installed capability exposes a user-facing activation/control in the app.
activationLegend.browser: Activation is provided by the browser/OS rather than an in-app control.
activationLegend.missing: Installed technically, but the user cannot yet activate/use the capability from the app.

governance.sharedLibraryAdoptionRule: Available or Tested/compatible never authorises a consuming-app repository change. Moving to Installed requires explicit user authorisation.
